extracted.intended_audience: researchers and academics considering volunteering as peer reviewers for PeerJ (Reviewer Match programme)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers who want to volunteer to review manuscripts through PeerJ's Reviewer Match programme, including how manuscripts are shown, selection constraints, and the review openness policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review openness / model
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this open peer review? No, peer review is still single-blind and all recommendations are private between the authors and Academic Editor. However, any reviewer has the option to sign their report, and once accepted for publication then that review can be shown publicly - again this is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should expect a single-blind process by default; they may optionally sign their report. If they sign and the paper is accepted the signed review can be made public, but signing is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteering is not a guarantee to be invited
rubrics_metrics.description: Will I be guaranteed to review if I volunteer? No. Volunteering is not a guarantee that you will be asked to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that volunteering expresses interest only; actual invitations depend on other selection criteria and editorial needs (see related criteria below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For one, reviewers must have relevant qualifications for any manuscript...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will only invite volunteers whose expertise and qualifications match the manuscript's subject and scope. Volunteers should assess whether their qualifications are a close fit before offering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: ...and void of any conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteers who have conflicts of interest with the manuscript (e.g., close collaborators, competitors, or other relevant relationships) should not expect to be invited; disclosing conflicts is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript availability depends on author opt-in and editorial recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Why aren't there more manuscripts available? Manuscripts are shown when authors have opted-in for obtaining reviewers through the reviewer-match service. Additionally, there may already be enough reviewers found through other means, for example, invitations sent by the Academic Editor in charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all submissions are listed via Reviewer Match; availability is conditional on authors opting in and on whether editors have already filled reviewer slots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-area / expertise matching (tag-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page displays subject areas and topic tags for manuscripts (e.g., data-mining-and-machine-learning, public-health, bioinformatics, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching between volunteers and manuscripts appears driven by these subject tags; volunteers should use subject areas to find manuscripts aligned with their expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial criteria reference
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the editorial criteria? Please visit the editorial criteria page for initial guidance. You will also be given additional information if invited to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial guidance about the journal's editorial/evaluation standards is provided on a separate editorial criteria page; invited reviewers receive further, manuscript-specific information and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional invitation-specific information
rubrics_metrics.description: You will also be given additional information if invited to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invited, expect to receive more detailed information about the manuscript, review expectations, deadlines, and any specific evaluation points from the Academic Editor.
